items.t: Fulton County may scan more than 1,000 early ballots again after equipment failures
items.sum: Fulton elections officials asked their board to approve rescanning 1,069 early ballots from two sites after one scanner kept reporting a phantom paper jam and another failed when its power cable was run over, with the work to be done in public view after polls closed on the advice of state voting-systems staff.

items.t: Georgia Democrats take PSC majority, setting up power bill fights
items.sum: Democrats Peter Hubbard and Shelia Edwards won the two Public Service Commission seats on the ballot, giving the party a 3-2 majority on Georgia Power's regulator for the first time in more than two decades after a campaign dominated by rising bills and data-center demand.

items.t: Keisha Lance Bottoms elected Georgia governor, a first for a Black woman in US
items.sum: Former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated Republican Rick Jackson, who spent more than $200 million of his own fortune, to become the first Black woman elected governor of any U.S. state and the first Democrat to win Georgia's top office since 1998.

items.t: LIVE UPDATES: Georgia elections 2026
items.sum: WSB's Election Day blog tracked more than 4.1 million votes cast, Justice Department monitors in six metro and coastal counties, brief disruptions at a Gwinnett precinct and a Barrow County machine audit, and the AP's race calls through the night.

items.t: Georgia voters issue their verdicts on 3 constitutional amendments
items.sum: Voters approved all three statewide amendments, expanding the acreage eligible for conservation-use farm and timber tax breaks, removing party labels from probate judge ballots, and letting the state dedicate money to modernize 911 systems.

items.t: U.S. Sen. Jon Ossoff cruises to reelection over Republican Mike Collins
items.sum: The AP called the Senate race for Democrat Jon Ossoff about an hour after polls closed, with early returns giving him roughly two-thirds of the vote over Rep. Mike Collins after Ossoff outraised him $136.6 million to $9.7 million.

items.t: Georgia voters head to polls with both parties anxious
items.sum: On the morning of the vote, Republicans were counting on a late Election Day surge to offset Democrats' early-voting edge while Democrats stayed cautiously optimistic about a possible statewide breakthrough.

items.t: Inside Democrats' push to flip the Georgia House
items.sum: The Democratic Party of Georgia put $2.1 million into ads and mail for 13 state House and three state Senate races and opened 29 field offices in a bid to net the 10 seats needed for a House majority, an outcome the AJC's Politically Georgia team still rated a long shot.

items.t: Race for Georgia governor draws more than $150 million in final three months
items.sum: Final pre-election disclosures showed Bottoms and self-funding Republican Rick Jackson together took in more than $150 million for the governor's race from Aug. 1 onward.

items.t: Josh McKoon won't seek another term as Georgia GOP chair
items.sum: Georgia Republican Party Chair Josh McKoon confirmed he will step down at the end of his second term, citing time with his family, leaving an open leadership contest likely to be fought on the party's right flank.

items.t: 'Flip the switch': Obama rallies Clayton County voters as Georgia early voting nears end
items.sum: Former President Barack Obama headlined a Clayton County rally for Bottoms, Ossoff and the rest of the Democratic ticket in the final days of early voting, after President Trump held two rallies in Georgia earlier in the month.

items.t: Georgia Ponzi schemer gets 15 years for $76 million fraud
items.sum: A federal judge sentenced Edwin Brant Frost IV, head of the Newnan-based conservative lender First Liberty, to 15 years in prison for a Ponzi scheme that cost more than 300 investors about $76 million.
